name: A Cape Town garden

place_source.title: Wikidata: Cape Town (Q5465), coordinate location and elevation above sea level

blurb: A walled garden on the lower slopes below Table Mountain in the winter-rainfall Cape: a lawn, aloes and agaves, a loquat and a palm, a stink-bean hedge, fynbos just above the wall. Cape bulbuls, white-eyes, apalises and sunbirds work the shrubs, red-winged starlings and helmeted guineafowl patrol the lawn, rock hyraxes claim the rock ridge. After dark a grey mongoose crosses the path.

facts.text: Cape Town has a hot-summer Mediterranean climate (Köppen Csa), with mild, moderately wet winters and dry, hot summers; winter runs from June to September and can bring large cold fronts off the Atlantic.

source.title: Wikipedia: Cape Town
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Cape Town", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The city's Mediterranean climate and its native fynbos mean winter is the rainy season, so a Cape Town garden's spring flowering and bird breeding run from about August to November.

source.title: Wikipedia: Cape Town
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Cape Town", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Cape Town is built where the Cape Fold Belt meets the Atlantic, with Table Mountain rising directly behind the city, so a single suburb spans sea level, the mountain's lower slopes and the fynbos above them.

source.title: Wikipedia: Cape Town
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Cape Town", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The red-winged starling has moved into cities and towns because the structure of tall buildings and houses works as a nest site like the cliffs it originally nested on, and it now breeds in roofs, apertures and under house eaves.

source.title: Wikipedia: Red-winged starling
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Red-winged starling", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The Cape grey mongoose lives in close association with people, often under the floors of outbuildings and on the fringe of suburbia, and when habituated to human presence may tolerate a close approach.

source.title: Wikipedia: Cape grey mongoose
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Cape grey mongoose", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Cape porcupines are nocturnal and monogamous, living as mated pairs that may share up to six burrows, and they eat mostly plant material - fruit, roots, tubers, bulbs and bark - which is why they are considered pests by some farmers.

source.title: Wikipedia: Cape porcupine
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Cape porcupine", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The western leopard toad is endemic to the low-lying areas of the Cape Peninsula and Cape Flats, and because much of its historic foraging habitat is now suburb it is often found living in suburban gardens, where it breeds in garden ponds.

source.title: Wikipedia: Western leopard toad
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Western leopard toad", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The Cape dwarf chameleon has lost most of its habitat to urbanisation and agriculture, and still shows as partly adaptable to suburban gardens, where it needs direct sun and fine twigs to climb.

source.title: Wikipedia: Cape dwarf chameleon
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Cape dwarf chameleon", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
